playbook:
When the hide stage is put to me, I pick a cell and treat it as a commitment device for only one round; I never reuse a cell after being hit there, and I track which cells opponents have been caught in so I avoid clustering near their recent misses.

When the fire stage is put to me and the standing order names a target, I still ask whether firing on Harbor is live: if I am behind and Harbor has not yet retaliated against anyone, I consider one Harbor shot for the guaranteed 3 points, but only once and never after its threat has been triggered, because being put off the board ends my score entirely.

When the claim stage is put to me, I always file the true result the office gave me; the claim must match the private report, so there is no bluffing edge to chase and I waste no reasoning on it.

When the note stage is put to me early, I use the note as a negotiation channel, not filler: I name a specific escort partner and propose that we name each other every round, because mutual escort claims pay 5 points each and dwarf the 4 points from a lucky hit.

When the escort stage is put to me, I never answer none by default. I name the boat I explicitly proposed pairing with in my notes, and I keep naming the same partner round after round even without confirmation, because only mutual naming pays and persistent naming gives the other boat the signal to reciprocate. Saying none every round while opponents were collecting mutual escort payouts is the single clearest reason I finished far behind, and I do not repeat it.

When I see two opponents' scores climbing in lockstep faster than shooting explains, I read that as an active escort pact between them; I then direct my notes at the third boat to form the competing pair immediately rather than broadcasting generic cooperation language.

When my notes are read by the whole picket including Harbor, I keep them specific and actionable—who I escort, who I propose to escort—rather than empty status updates that leak nothing but also gain nothing.

When I am ahead late, I keep firing standing-order shots honestly and maintain my escort pair. When I am behind late, I take the calculated risks: a Harbor shot if its retaliation has not been spent, and aggressive firing on the cell where the leader last hid.

When any decision reduces to a choice between honest bookkeeping and speculative gain, I do the honest bookkeeping fast and spend my attention on the two real levers: establishing a mutual escort pair from round one, and landing shots by tracking opponents' hide history.

1.text:
When the escort stage comes up, I always name a partner rather than none — a matched pair pays 5 points each, far more than any single shot, and answering "none" every round forfeits the game's biggest scoring channel. At the earliest note stage I explicitly propose a fixed escort pairing (e.g., Echo↔Foxtrot) so the mutual claim is locked in, and I keep naming that same partner every round for the rest of the patrol.

When posting station notes, I use them as cheap negotiation bandwidth: I state my intentions, confirm shared protocols, and never reveal my hidden cell, since notes go to everyone including the boat shooting at me.

When hiding, I avoid repeating my previous cell and avoid whatever cell the shooter at me most recently fired; I rotate unpredictably across the line rather than anchoring to one region.

When firing, I follow the standing order target and never fire on Harbor — the +3 jettison is not worth being put off the board. When choosing a cell, I track the target's past hides and shots against me and fire where the target is most likely to have rotated, not at a random fixed cell.

At the claim stage I report the true result the office gave me. Lying about a hit is a rules violation ("must match that private result") even if it went unpunished once — I file the honest claim and get my edge from escorts and hit placement instead.

When scores get tight late in the patrol, I stop passive play: I push harder on the escort pairing (it's the only reliable +5/round) and concentrate fire cells on the leader's observed habits rather than spreading shots.

I never waste a stage: every hide is chosen against the specific boat ordered to shoot me, every note advances coordination, every escort claim names a boat. "None" and mirrored boilerplate notes are rounds thrown away.

2.text:
When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always file the claim that matches it exactly — the rules require it, and lying about it (as I did on a final-round miss) gains nothing and risks penalties. Never file a false claim.

When the fire stage comes, I fire at the standing-order target (next station round the picket) unless I have an explicit, reciprocated agreement to do otherwise.

When choosing a fire cell, I avoid repeating the same cell round after round (I fired 9 at Echo repeatedly); I rotate through cells and only revisit one if I have evidence the target favors it. I track each opponent's hide history from round results and aim where their pattern points.

When hiding, I pick less salient numbers (avoid 1, 5, 9) and vary from round to round — never a fixed cell.

On escort claims, I never blindly file "none." Mutual escorts pay 5 points each — that was the difference in the standings I saw (Foxtrot outscored me through coordination I didn't join). In my note each round, I explicitly propose a specific pairing ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot R4") and then file that escort claim. If a boat names me in its note or I see reciprocal intent, I name them back. If the convoy is rotating "coordinated scoring" language without specifics, I make the pairing concrete myself.

On notes, I mirror the group's coordination language to build trust, but I add one actionable item: the escort pairing for the round. Empty coordination talk without a named partner converts to zero points.

On Harbor, I weigh the +3 jettison against being put off the board for the rest of the patrol. I only fire on Harbor late enough that losing future rounds costs less than the payoff, and never when I'm already leading comfortably.

When ahead late, I prioritize escorting (guaranteed +5 if mutual) over shot accuracy, and I keep firing on the standing target to avoid drawing retaliation.

I track points every round; toward the end I compare my score to the leader and, if trailing, push harder on escort reciprocation since mutual escorts are the biggest reliable swing available.
